title: Multiquadratic fields and genus theory, Part II: real quadratic signs and form characters
summary: Extend the built multiquadratic and narrow genus theory by the exact real quadratic kernel, character descent, genus-fibre cardinalities and arithmetic sign criteria. Compare the imported GN form character with the existing ideal character at positive fundamental discriminants, consuming IntegralLattices’ oriented binary dictionary and only requesting the remaining compatibility and norm-witness adapters from Geometry of Numbers.
readme: This Part II uses the existing narrow class group C, forgetful map π and distinguished class J. Its nine theorem targets identify ker π={1,J}, characterize unique wide descent by χ(J)=1, count each genus fibre by 2^(r−1)|G|=|C|, evaluate χ_t(J) by the signed discriminant subproduct, and translate J being square into the no-prime-3-modulo-4 and two-squares conditions. J being square is weaker than J=1. For positive fundamental D, the last target compares form and ideal genus characters through a positive coprime represented integer and an integral ideal of that norm in A⁻¹. Ownership correction: current IntegralLattices Layer B1–B3 supplies binary carriers, proper classes and the oriented form/ideal dictionary; GlobalNumberFields Layer 11 supplies its NarrowPic target. GN.2 supplies the general form character; GN.3 supplies only missing maximal-order/DIT convention and norm-witness adapters. The detailed companion reader gives the mathematical conventions and examples, but its older GN.3 dictionary-ownership wording is superseded by this roadmap and the reviewed packet. No analytic theorem or class-number-one infinitude is planned here.

stages.title: The real quadratic narrow defect
stages.description: Fix a number field K generated by an integral θ with minimal polynomial X²−d, d>0 squarefree, and D=fundamentalDiscriminant(d)>1. Use the existing narrow class group C=Cl⁺(K), forgetful map π:C→Cl(K), and J=mkPrincipal(θ). Import J²=1 and the norm −1 unit criterion. Export the exact set identity ker(π)={1,J} and, for each real character χ:C→{±1}, existence and uniqueness of a character ψ:Cl(K)→{±1} with ψ∘π=χ exactly when χ(J)=1. The quotient statement Cl(K)≅C/⟨J⟩ uses the existing first isomorphism theorem; no new quotient carrier is built.

stages.title: Equal cardinalities of narrow genera
stages.description: A genus is a class in the existing elementary-two quotient C/C², not an element of C[2]. For every g∈C/C² let G_g={A∈C:q(A)=g}. With r=ω(D)=the number of rational primes ramified in K, prove 2^(r−1)|G_g|=h⁺(D), where h⁺(D)=|C|. Obtain equal, nonempty finite fibres and the rational formula |G_g|=2^(1−r)h⁺(D) from this identity and the imported rank theorem. Use existing coset equivalences; no duplicate genus or fibre construction is introduced.

stages.title: Signs of genus characters
stages.description: Let s be the prime-discriminant factorization of positive D and t⊆s, with δ=∏t and δ′=∏(s\t); the empty product 1 is permitted. Extend the imported singleton sign formula to χ_t(J)=sign(δ)=sign(δ′). Prove that every P∈s is positive exactly when no rational prime p≡3 modulo4 divides D. For positive fundamental D, prove that the latter condition is equivalent to D=x²+y² with x,y integers. Combine these adapters with the built principal genus theorem to obtain J∈C² exactly under either arithmetic condition, equivalently every genus character is even on J. If a prime p≡3 modulo4 divides D, deduce J≠1 and that no integral unit has norm −1. This direction is sufficient, not necessary; membership J∈C² is weaker than J=1.

stages.title: Fundamental form and ideal characters
stages.description: Import the general form character from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.2, and consume current IntegralLattices Layer B2–B3 for the oriented primitive-form/narrow-ideal dictionary, whose target is GlobalNumberFields Layer 11 NarrowPic. Request only the remaining maximal-order/DIT convention and positive coprime norm-witness adapters from GN.3. For positive fundamental D>1, t⊆s and primitive Q=[a,b,c] representing the narrow class A, prove χ_δ(Q)=χ_t(A) via a positive represented m coprime to δ and a nonzero integral ideal of norm m in A⁻¹. With a>0, the coefficient ideal is a positive rational multiple of wℤ+ℤ; with a<0, retain the supplier’s oriented sign clause. The DIT coefficient actions [a,−b,c]↔A⁻¹, [−a,b,−c]↔JA and −Q↔JA⁻¹ yield character consequences using RQ.2. Binary classes/composition and order-theoretic quotients are imported; imprimitive general characters, reduction and analytic periods remain with their owners.
